## HEAD

**Operator-voice anchor** (Joe, 2026-09-26, `*claude-repl:claude-14*`, verbatim):

> Right, well speaking of 象, I had been discussing a 象-2000 implementation of
> McCarthy's Elephant-2000 ideas, and the xlate stuff that feeds into feed.html
> would be a great data source.  The result of being able to rewind to a given
> place in a development cycle etc. (e.g. to right before red tape started) and
> debug how it came to be would be very cool.

**Provenance:** operator turn in the claude-14 REPL, 2026-09-26 ~02:50 UTC,
following a discussion of the @why graph and the pattern-mining run. Earlier
象-2000 discussion: the 象/ pattern family (futon3 `10643d9`, `b871428`),
seeded from turn-Ogz2uU (2026-09-23): "we have XTDB, so we have an as-of
database; this is basically the infrastructure needed to build Elephant 2000".

**HEAD exit: Met.**
The operator's anchor turn is recorded verbatim above.

---

fragments.target: the HEAD section of the mission file
fragments.rationale: Structural section marker; it frames everything below as the mission's opening position rather than contributing operator content.
fragments.no_surface_cue: pure structural heading; there is no operator move to cue

fragments.target: the operator turn that anchors the mission
fragments.rationale: The HEAD declares what it is anchored to: a verbatim operator turn with seat and date. The mission binds itself to the source bytes of a specific turn rather than to a paraphrase of intent.

pattern_refs.rationale: The anchor is quoted verbatim and labelled verbatim: the mission's authority is derived by citing the exact source bytes of the turn, not by summarising them.

fragments.text: Right, well speaking of 象, I had been discussing a 象-2000 implementation of
fragments.rationale: Joe opens by locating the move in an ongoing conversation ('speaking of 象', 'I had been discussing') — context-setting before the proposal, not the proposal itself.

fragments.target: McCarthy's Elephant-2000 as the named lineage
fragments.rationale: Joe names the intellectual family the implementation belongs to. 象-2000 is presented as a member of the Elephant-2000 family, not a novel invention.

pattern_refs.rationale: 象-2000 is named as a protocol-family instance: Elephant-2000 is the family shape, 象-2000 the local implementation.

fragments.text: the xlate stuff that feeds into feed.html
fragments.rationale: Joe points at an existing, running seam — the xlate pipeline — as the resource for the new work, rather than commissioning fresh instrumentation.

pattern_refs.rationale: The move is to build on the seam that already exists and already feeds a surface (feed.html), fitting the new capability to existing infrastructure instead of forking it.

fragments.text: would be a great data source.
fragments.target: xlate as the data source for 象-2000
fragments.rationale: Joe's judgement on the identified seam: it is not merely usable but 'great'. The endorsement is what converts the xlate pipeline from background plumbing into the mission's named input.

fragments.text: The result of being able to rewind to a given
fragments.rationale: Joe names the desired capability: rewinding to an arbitrary earlier point. This is the leading edge of the goal clause that completes across the next two lines.

pattern_refs.rationale: Rewinding to a given place is exactly the as-of query over bitemporal records: valid time and system time let the cycle be re-entered at any point.

fragments.text: place in a development cycle etc. (e.g. to right before red tape started) and
fragments.target: the granularity and use of the rewind
fragments.rationale: Joe grounds the abstract rewind in a concrete scenario — re-entering the cycle right before red tape started. The parenthetical is doing the work: rewind exists so a specific historical moment can be re-inhabited.

pattern_refs.rationale: A rewound state is a view rebuilt from history, not a snapshot that was saved in advance: the cycle position before red tape is reconstructible because the history is the source of truth.

fragments.text: debug how it came to be would be very cool.
fragments.rationale: The point of the rewind is diagnosis: 'debug how it came to be' asks for the causal chain that produced a state, and 'very cool' is Joe's explicit value signal on that capability.

pattern_refs.rationale: The rewind is valued as a debugging instrument: trace how a state came to be from its evidence, which is invariant-4 debugging applied to development history.
'How it came to be' is a request to make the causal chain behind a state explicit rather than leaving it implicit in the record.

pattern_rejections.reason: About periodic point-in-time projections kept as standing evidence; the anchor wants rewind-and-debug over full event history, not a snapshot cadence.
pattern_rejections.query: as-of database rewind time travel history

fragments.text: **Provenance:** operator turn in the claude-14 REPL, 2026-09-26 ~02:50 UTC,
fragments.target: the provenance of the anchor turn
fragments.rationale: The HEAD records where the anchor came from — seat, time — so the mission's authority trace is inspectable. This is the recording of what was consulted.

pattern_refs.rationale: The mission records exactly which artifact it consulted (operator turn, claude-14 REPL, timestamp) so later readers can trust the citation per artifact.

fragments.text: following a discussion of the @why graph and the pattern-mining run. Earlier
fragments.target: the conversational context of the anchor turn
fragments.rationale: Locates the anchor within its session — it followed the @why graph and pattern-mining discussion — connective tissue between the provenance block and the lineage block that follows.

fragments.text: 象-2000 discussion: the 象/ pattern family (futon3 `10643d9`, `b871428`),
fragments.target: the 象/ pattern family as prior art
fragments.rationale: The lineage of the idea is cited by commit hash rather than re-explained: the 象/ family already exists in the library and the mission stands on it.

pattern_refs.rationale: The past discussion is cited by reference (family name plus commit hashes) instead of being repeated — the past need not be restated, only cited.

fragments.text: seeded from turn-Ogz2uU (2026-09-23): "we have XTDB, so we have an as-of
fragments.rationale: The lineage is traced one step further back, to the specific turn that seeded the family, and the seed's own words begin to be quoted.

fragments.text: database; this is basically the infrastructure needed to build Elephant 2000".
fragments.target: the seed turn's rationale: XTDB as-of as the Elephant-2000 substrate
fragments.rationale: The quoted seed states the load-bearing claim: the as-of database is already the infrastructure Elephant 2000 needs. The mission HEAD inherits this rationale rather than re-arguing it.

pattern_refs.rationale: The quoted claim is precisely 双时并记's premise: with bitemporal as-of records (XTDB), the rewind substrate already exists.

pattern_rejections.reason: Rational reconstruction rebuilds rationale after the fact; the HEAD holds the seed's verbatim words and wants causal debugging on recorded history, not reconstruction of intent.

fragments.rationale: The mission declares its own opening gate satisfied: the anchor turn exists and is recorded. A status declaration, not an operator request.

fragments.text: The operator's anchor turn is recorded verbatim above.
fragments.target: the scope of what the HEAD claims
fragments.rationale: The HEAD closes by scoping its own claim: it records the anchor verbatim and nothing more. It asserts provenance of the desire, not that any desired outcome has happened.

pattern_refs.rationale: The closing sentence restates the discipline: the claim is backed by the recorded bytes above, verbatim, with nothing extrapolated beyond them.

fragments.rationale: Structural separator closing the HEAD section.
fragments.no_surface_cue: pure structural separator; no operator move to cue
